text.p: Southdown Inc said Wednesday it would complete the expansion of its cement-making facilities in Fairborn, Ohio, and Victorville, Calif., this summer, boosting capacity by 400,000 tons.
It said it would bring on line other projects by the middle of 1998 to add another 300,000 tons of cement capacity.

"Production from these projects will service the growth in cement consumption and construction activity in the California market and other regions of the country," it said. "Currently, U.S. cement demand is well ahead of last year's record levels."
Southdown has annual cement capacity of more than six million tons, making it one of the largest producers in the U.S.
The company today reported second quarter operating profits of $1.04 per diluted share, up from $0.79 a year earlier.
